data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'mutamana' meaning to believe, trust or have faith. The name Mutamin signifies a person who is steadfast in his faith and beliefs. In the Quran, this name is used for a believer who is assured of Allah's mercy and forgiveness. The name Mutamin carries the meaning “Believer, Confident” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mutamin usually hope their child will grow to embody believer, confident and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hajar al-Haytami, in his work Al-Fatawa al-Hadirah, mentions a group of scholars known as 'As-Sabiqun Al-Mutaminnun' or 'The Constant Ones'. This term was used to describe a group of scholars who were known for their unwavering commitment to the Sunna and their rejection of innovations in religion. They lived during the early Ottoman period, primarily in the 16th century.

Al-Qalqashandi, in his book Subh as-Sittah fi Tarikh al-Quds, records the existence of a scholar named Mutamin ibn Saeed, who was a prominent figure in the Ayyubid period. Mutamin was known for his extensive knowledge of Islamic jurisprudence and his ability to memorize and recite the Quran. He lived in Egypt during the late 13th and early 14th centuries.
